big_case.notes: Whether corporate registration under a statute lacking explicit consent language satisfies Fourteenth Amendment due process post-Mallory is doctrinally significant in the abstract, and the $10.86M default judgment mattered to the parties, but this petition was a severely flawed vehicle — arising from an intrastate Georgia battery injury where the Georgia Court of Appeals ruled solely on state-law venue and untimely default-opening without addressing personal jurisdiction, compounded by unwithdrawn specific-jurisdiction admissions — and ended in a routine summary cert denial with one amicus brief and no dissent.
